title: How deep is the deepest part of the ocean?
sources: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution Hadal Zone

lines.text: How deep is the deepest, darkest point on our entire planet?
lines.caps: How deep is the *deepest point | on planet *Earth?

lines.text: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench plunges nearly thirty-six thousand feet into the abyss.
lines.caps: Plunges nearly *36,000 feet | into the freezing *abyss

lines.text: If you took Mount Everest and placed it at the bottom, its highest snowy peak would still be over a mile underwater.
lines.caps: Mount Everest would be *over | a mile *underwater!

lines.text: At this depth, water pressure reaches over sixteen thousand pounds per square inch.
lines.caps: Water pressure exceeds *16,000 pounds | per *square inch

lines.text: That is equivalent to having fifty jumbo jet airplanes stacked directly on your chest.
lines.caps: Like 50 *jumbo jet airplanes | resting on your *chest

lines.text: Yet despite crushing pressure and absolute blackness, translucent ghost fish and amphipods thrive here.
We know vastly more about the craters on the Moon than the floor of our own oceans.
lines.caps: We know more about the *Moon | than our deep *oceans!
